transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Well, I'm here because... well, it’s my job, really. I’m a building cleaner, have been for years, and lately, things have just gotten completely out of hand. It’s the rats. Or, well, not even just the rats themselves, but the thought of them. Just the idea that I might see one. It’s gotten so bad that I literally can’t do parts of my job anymore. I mean, I know logically that it’s just an old building, or a trash room, and they’re probably more scared of me than I am of them, and it’s not really dangerous, but I just... I can't. 

Like, the other day, I was supposed to go down to the basement level of this one office building to clear out the recycling bins, and just standing at the top of the stairs, my heart started pounding so hard I thought I was going to have a heart attack. I kept picturing one scurrying across the floor, or worse, jumping out of a bin. I ended up having to ask my supervisor to do it, which was so embarrassing. I pride myself on being a hard worker, you know? I’ve always done my fair share and then some. But now, if I even think there’s a chance a rat might be around, I just freeze. I can’t sleep the night before I know I have to clean the older buildings on my route. I just lie awake thinking about it. It’s ruining my life, honestly, and I’m terrified I’m going to lose my job if I keep refusing to do certain tasks. I just don't know what to do anymore.

Have you ever had sudden, intense episodes of fear or physical discomfort, like a racing heart, sweating, or feeling like you’re losing control, specifically when you’re in a place where you think rats might be?

Oh, absolutely. It’s... it’s exactly like that. It's not just a little nervous feeling, it's like a complete takeover of my body. Like, just last Tuesday, I was in the utility closet on the ground floor of the Miller building—which is already a nightmare because the lighting in there is terrible, just this one flickering fluorescent bulb that management refuses to fix—and I swear I heard this tiny scratching sound. Just a little noise near the baseboard, right where the drywall meets the concrete floor. 

And, you know, if I hear scratching near a wall like that, or, God forbid, if I see even a shadow move by a water pipe... my whole body just reacts right away. I mean instantly. It’s like a switch flips in my brain. My heart just starts pounding out of my chest, so hard I can actually hear it rushing in my ears, and my hands start shaking so badly I can't even hold onto my cleaning supplies. The spray bottles, the rags, they just fall right out of my hands. And this overwhelming feeling hits me where I just feel like I have to get out, like I have to run away before I can even think straight. 

I don’t even process what I'm doing in those moments, I just know I need to be on the other side of that door, out in the hallway where it's safe. I remember backing up so fast that day that I knocked over a mop bucket, and dirty water went everywhere, ruining the floor I had just swept, but I couldn't even bring myself to care. I just had to escape. It's just so immediate and so intense. I can't control it at all.
Do you ever experience these intense episodes of fear or physical discomfort when you're not in a situation where rats or reminders of rats are present?

No, no, never. It's really just the rats. I mean, if I'm at home, sitting in my living room watching TV—and I live on the fourth floor of a pretty well-maintained apartment building, so we don't really have those kinds of issues there, thank goodness, because I don't know what I would do if I couldn't even feel safe in my own home. But yeah, if I'm just at home, or at the grocery store, or out walking my sister's dog in the park... I'm completely fine. My heart is fine, I'm not sweating, I'm not shaking. I'm just a normal person going about my day. 

It really is only when I'm at work, or specifically in those parts of the buildings where I know they might be. Like the basements, the trash rooms, the loading docks... those dark, damp places. Or even if I'm just driving to work and I know I have to clean the Miller building that day, I might start feeling a little tense, but that full-blown panic, that feeling like I'm going to jump out of my skin and I have to run for my life? That only happens when I'm right there, in the thick of it, and I hear a noise or see a shadow that makes me think one is close by. If there's no chance of a rat being around, I don't get those feelings at all. Not even a little bit. It's so strange how specific it is, isn't it? Like my body only has this extreme reaction to this one very specific thing, but when it happens, it's just so overpowering.
